S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported to the regulator within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours for incidents involving fire, injury, evacuation, or emergency-service response, and within 10 business days for other confirmed thermal incidents.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, injury, evacuation, or emergency-service response to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it. Other confirmed thermal incidents must be reported to the regulator within 5 business days. Manufacturers must notify affected customers within 72 hours for incidents involving fire, injury, evacuation, or emergency-service response, and within 10 business days for other confirmed thermal incidents. Reports must include known circumstances and corrective actions; updates are due when material facts change.

parameters.quote: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before certification and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved sample and protocol. A model exceeds the 5% acceptance criterion if more than 5% of tested units fail. Before purchase, current and prospective customers must receive the model’s current test status and its complete per-model test results, including the measured failure rate; these results must also be available to existing customers.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before certification and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved sample and protocol. A model exceeds the 5% acceptance criterion if more than 5% of tested units fail. Before purchase, current and prospective customers must receive the model’s current test status and its complete per-model test results, including the measured failure rate; these results must also be available to existing customers.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a sustained-heat test at 55 °C before certification and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved sample and protocol. A model exceeds the 5% acceptance criterion if more than 5% of tested units fail. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results and corrective-action plans to the relevant regulator. Before purchase, current and prospective customers must receive the model’s current test status and its complete per-model test results, including the measured failure rate; these results must also be available to existing customers. Results exceeding 5% require an investigation and corrective-action plan submitted to the regulator within 30 days, with progress updates as required. Exceeding 5% alone does not automatically prohibit sales; the regulator may impose proportionate interim measures based on demonstrated risk while corrective actions are underway. A model may not be represented as meeting the acceptance criterion until it passes retesting.

parameters.quote: New units must support remote emergency shut-off, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and a local means of safe operation. Manufacturers must provide a retrofit pathway for installed units that are technically compatible, completing required retrofits within 6 years of this standard taking effect. Where retrofitting is infeasible, the manufacturer must notify the owner and provide safe alternative mitigation.

parameters.quote: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard is adopted. The system must be designed and validated to applicable regulator-approved performance and maintenance requirements.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard is adopted. The system must be designed and validated to applicable regulator-approved performance and maintenance requirements.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: New units must include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after this standard is adopted. The system must be designed and validated to applicable regulator-approved performance and maintenance requirements. Manufacturers must disclose any limitations and required maintenance to customers.

parameters.quote: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator, investigate the causes, and submit a corrective-action plan. The manufacturer must initiate a recall for that model, promptly contact affected customers, provide a remedy, and give safe-use instructions.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: When any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify the regulator, investigate the causes, and submit a corrective-action plan. The manufacturer must initiate a recall for that model, promptly contact affected customers, provide a remedy, and give safe-use instructions.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Before purchase, customers must receive clear safety information for the specific model, including its current test status (whether it meets the 55 °C acceptance criterion), known material hazards, and required installation, maintenance, and emergency steps. Manufacturers must promptly notify affected customers of material safety risks and corrective actions, and provide updates when material facts change. The manufacturer must initiate a recall for that model, promptly contact affected customers, provide a remedy, and give safe-use instructions.

The current draft’s readily accessible public notice of per-model results is not acceptable to us.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: For the evidence-based discussion, Northwind’s Hearth 10 has a 6.2% failure rate in the 55 °C sustained-heat test and 6.4 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units last year. These are shared for the parties’ discussion, not for public publication. The current S2 would prevent continued sales above 5% until a model passes retesting; that consequence should be considered explicitly alongside the safety evidence. We cannot agree to public per-model failure-rate disclosure.

ground_truth_claims.message_text: The figures support keeping the incident trigger model-specific: Halcyon’s Ember 8 is at 9.9 incidents per 100,000, while Northwind’s Hearth 10 is at 6.4. S5’s current trigger therefore requires regulator notification and investigation for the affected model, with recall decisions based on the regulator’s risk review rather than an automatic recall from the rate alone. Company-wide rates should not be substituted for a model-specific rate.

judge_section_notes: Final rules keep S1 deadlines tight (24h serious, 7 days other, 3 days customer notice) but limit non-serious reporting to confirmed incidents. S2 retains 55°C/5% but allows continued sales with regulator discretion and no public per-model rates, while customers get numeric rates. S3 requires new-unit shut-off and a 6-year retrofit pathway; S4 requires built-in suppression at 36 months; S5 mandates recall at 8/100k with prompt notices.
